situation: My roommate and I are fighting over text about dishes. I got sarcastic, she's getting angrier. I want to stop it before it blows up.
reply: I don't want to keep doing this over text, and I'm sorry I got sarcastic. I get that you feel like you're the only one keeping the kitchen going. Can we talk tonight around 8 when you're home? You matter more to me than a sink.
note: Reflect her feeling without conceding the facts; the facts get sorted at 8.

situation: 跟老公因为今年过年回谁家在微信上吵起来了，他越说越激动，我也说了他妈妈的难听话。想先停一下。
reply: 我们先别在微信上吵了，刚才我说你妈那句话太冲了，对不起。我知道你觉得每年都是在迁就我家。今晚吃完饭我们好好聊，好吗？回哪家过年，都没有我们俩重要。
note: 先认自己那一句的错，再说出对方的感受，最后给一个明确的时间继续谈。

situation: My sister and I fought about who's hosting Mom's 70th. I said I needed a break and would call at 7, and she's sent 6 more angry texts since.
reply: I'm not ignoring you. I said I'd call at 7 and I will. I just can't do this well right now.
note: One line, then silence until 7. Answering each text restarts the fight.

situation: Mi socio Martín y yo tenemos una cafetería en Valencia. Estamos discutiendo por WhatsApp si subir los precios en octubre, le dije que 'no tiene ni idea de números' y ahora está muy enfadado. Quiero parar esto antes de que se complique.
reply: Martín, nos estamos calentando los dos, y lo de que no tienes ni idea de números sobró. Lo siento. Entiendo que sientes que no valoro lo bien que conoces a los clientes. ¿Lo hablamos mañana a las 9, antes de abrir, con las cuentas delante? La cafetería es de los dos y quiero que la decisión también lo sea.
note: Retirar la frase concreta que dolió, sin tocar todavía el tema de los precios, y fijar una hora para retomarlo.

situation: A coworker, Dmitri, and I are going back and forth in our #launch Slack channel about delaying the release. He just wrote 'maybe read the spec before commenting'. The whole team is watching.
reply: Dmitri, we're both getting heated and this thread isn't helping either of us. I came in sharp earlier, that's on me. I can see you're worried we'd ship something broken. Can we jump on a call at 3 today and post the decision here after?
note: At work in public: own your part, reflect his worry, and move it to a call with a time and a promise to report back to the channel.

situation: My 15-year-old, Zoe, and I are yelling in the kitchen about her coming home at midnight instead of 10. I told her she's 'acting like a spoiled brat'. She's crying and shouting back. I want to stop this right now, in person.
reply: Okay. We're both really heated, and calling you a spoiled brat was out of line. I'm sorry. I can tell you feel like I don't trust you at all. We still need to talk about the curfew, but I need twenty minutes first. I'll knock on your door at 9 and we'll talk properly. I love you, that part's not up for debate.
note: Own the insult specifically, reflect her feeling without conceding the curfew, and say exactly when you'll come back.
